          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 2.72 active sessions, 36.03% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is 2.17 active sessions, 28.68% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "9hn2a6m3vc7wp".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 9hn2a6m3vc7wp.
         INSERT INTO GLBKPL.TMPCONSLOAN11 (ACMASTCODE,AC_NO,RECPNL )   SELECT
         A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_NO,NVL(SUM(B.CREDIT),:"SYS_B_00") AS RECPNL
         FROM GLBKPL.TMPCONSLOAN5 A, GLBKPL.TMPCONSVIEWPROC54 B,ACMAST C
         WHERE A.ACMASTCODE=C.ACMASTCODE AND C.PNLACMCD=B.ACMASTCODE
         AND A.ACMASTCODE=B.REF_ACMCD AND A.AC_NO=B.REF_ACNO AND
         NVL(B.TRNTYPE,:"SYS_B_01")<>:"SYS_B_02"
         AND (NVL(B.SRCOFTRN,:"SYS_B_03")=:"SYS_B_04"  OR
         NVL(B.SRCOFTRN,:"SYS_B_05")=:"SYS_B_06" OR
         NVL(B.SRCOFTRN,:"SYS_B_07")=:"SYS_B_08" OR
         NVL(B.SRCOFTRN,:"SYS_B_09")=:"SYS_B_10" OR
         (NVL(B.TRNTYPE,:"SYS_B_11")=:"SYS_B_12" AND CSH_TRN=:"SYS_B_13")
         OR NVL(C.NPATYPPST,:"SYS_B_14")=:"SYS_B_15" OR
         NVL(C.INTPOSTREQ,:"SYS_B_16")=:"SYS_B_17" OR
         ((NVL(C.MICROFINANCE,:"SYS_B_18")=:"SYS_B_19"
         OR :"SYS_B_20" =:"SYS_B_21")   AND
         NVL(B.SRCOFTRN,:"SYS_B_22")=:"SYS_B_23"))
         AND C.IPST_ACMCD<>C.PNLACMCD
         GROUP BY A.ACMASTCODE,A.AC_NO
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 100% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "9hn2a6m3vc7wp" was executed 3 times and had
      an average elapsed time of 2227 seconds.
   Rationale
      Top level calls to execute the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID
      "64nr52qnkutha" are responsible for 100% of the database time spent on
      the INSERT statement with SQL_ID "9hn2a6m3vc7wp".
      Related Object

Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.08 active sessions, 14.32% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.08 active sessions, 14.32% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is .71 active sessions, 9.4% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .71 active sessions, 9.4% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .71 active sessions, 9.4% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .31 active sessions, 4.04% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .31 active sessions, 4.04% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .58 active sessions, 7.62% of total activity.


Finding 5: Java Execution
Impact is .17 active sessions, 2.21% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
JAVA execution consumed significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .17 active sessions, 2.21% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time in Java execution. For example, the PL/SQL statement
      with SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb" is responsible for 100% of Java execution
      time during the analysis period.


Finding 6: Unusual "Other" Wait Event

-------------------------------------------------------

          Findings and Recommendations

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.29 active sessions, 17.62% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.29 active sessions, 17.62% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is .97 active sessions, 13.2% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .97 active sessions, 13.2% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .97 active sessions, 13.2% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.
